scope: Matched zero-shot versus flower-task LoRA ablation on one synthetic held-out contact clip
summary: The smoke LoRA slightly improves three synthetic proxy scores but remains nearly identical to zero-shot and has poor absolute similarity, so it does not justify full real-video generation.
evidence: Contact-ROI similarity changes from 0.1319105 to 0.1344367 and contact-motion similarity from 0.5559492 to 0.5591135.
Global similarity changes only from 0.0839077 to 0.0840541, and zero-shot versus adapted mean absolute difference is 1.607 RGB levels.
Matched outputs use the same held-out target, trajectory, prompt, seed 20260811, 17 frames, and 20 inference steps.
lessons: Tiny positive proxy deltas from a smoke LoRA are insufficient when absolute visual fidelity remains poor.
A real critical-window gate is necessary before spending compute on a full long video.
limitations: The held-out clip is procedural synthetic data and pixel similarity is not flower-contact physics evidence.
next_actions: Evaluate a localized real interaction window with identical zero-shot and adapted settings.
